key_facts: Lesions are limited to the right axilla
Severe pruritus wakes the patient up at night
No recent trauma or history of similar lesions
No associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms
No improvement with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, or discontinuation of underarm deodorant
Biopsy findings show lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of discrete, dark red, circular lesions in the axilla with severe pruritus and biopsy findings showing lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction are consistent with inverse lichen planus, which typically affects intertriginous areas and presents with violaceous, annular patches.

rejected.label: lichen planus pigmentosus
rejected.why: Lichen planus pigmentosus typically presents with diffuse hyperpigmentation, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: lichenoid drug eruption
rejected.why: There is no mention of new medications or exposure to potential allergens that could trigger a lichenoid drug eruption.

rejected.label: atopic dermatitis
rejected.why: Atopic dermatitis typically presents with a history of atopy, eczematous lesions, and a more widespread distribution, which is not consistent with this case.

rejected.label: contact dermatitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms did not improve with discontinuation of underarm deodorant, making contact dermatitis less likely.

rejected.label: discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Discoid lupus erythematosus typically presents with scarring lesions, which are not described in this case, and the biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis.
